chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

From a man who appointed an agent to finalize a matter among the matters and witnessed him with two witnesses. The agent stood up and left to finalize the matter, and said: 'Bear witness that I have dismissed so-and-so from the agency.' He (the Imam) said: 'If the agent finalized the matter he was appointed for before the dismissal from the agency reached him, then the matter is valid and executed according to what the agent finalized, whether the principal disliked it or was pleased.' I said: 'If the agent finalized the matter before he knew of the dismissal or before it reached him that he had been dismissed from the agency, then the matter is executed according to what he finalized.' He said: 'Yes.' I said to him: 'If the dismissal reached him before he finalized the matter, then he went and finalized it, that would not be anything (valid).' He said: 'Yes. Indeed, when the agent is appointed, then he stands from the session, his matter remains valid forever, and the agency is established until the dismissal from the agency reaches him through a trustworthy person who informs him or by direct conversation regarding the dismissal from the agency.'
ai.seo_question: When does an agent's dismissal take effect in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal principle that an agent’s authority persists until formal notification of dismissal reaches them, ensuring transactional stability. It distinguishes between actions completed before notification, which remain binding, and those attempted after, which are void, reflecting the Shia emphasis on clear evidentiary standards in commercial contracts. This ruling underscores the importance of reliable communication channels (*thiqa*) in validating legal changes in agency status.
